target: def Target : Prop := ∀ T : Set Form, Def14 T (neg (ex 1 (K Def16)))
a_raw: {"translation": "Target is the proposition asserting that for every set of formulas T (with no restriction on T), the formula ¬ ∃x₁ K (∀x₀ (K (¬ R₀(x₀, x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁, x₀))) is derivable from T in the proof system Def14. More precisely, in the formal language Form (built from binary atomic formulas atom r x y indexed by natural numbers r, x, y, falsity fls, implication imp, universal quantification all x, and the unary operator K, with ¬φ defined as imp φ fls, φ ∧ ψ as ¬(imp φ (¬ψ)), φ ↔ ψ as (imp φ ψ) ∧ (imp ψ φ), and ∃x φ as ¬(all x (¬φ))), the derived formula is neg (ex 1 (K (all 0 (iff (K (neg (atom 0 0 0))) (atom 0 1 0))))), where R₀ denotes the relation with index 0, variable 0 is bound by the universal quantifier, variable 1 is bound by the existential quantifier, and the second atomic subformula has variable 1 as its first argument and variable 0 as its second argument. Derivability from T (Def14 T φ) means that φ belongs to the smallest set of formulas containing every formula in T and every axiom in Def13, and closed under modus ponens (from imp φ ψ and φ, infer ψ), with no other inference rules. Here Def13 consists of every formula obtainable by applying zero or more universal generalizations (all x) to a base axiom in Def11, together with every formula of the form K ψ where ψ is so obtainable (at most one outer application of K to such universally generalized base axioms). The base axioms (Def11) are: (1) all propositional tautologies (formulas true under every valuation v : Form → Prop with ¬ v fls and v (imp φ ψ) ↔ (v φ → v ψ)); (2) universal instantiation imp (all x φ) φ[y/x] whenever y is free for x in φ (where φ[y/x] replaces free occurrences of x with y); (3) quantifier distribution imp (all x (imp φ ψ)) (imp (all x φ) (all x ψ)); (4) vacuous quantification imp φ (all x φ) whenever x does not occur free in φ; (5) imp (K (imp φ ψ)) (imp (K φ) (K ψ)); (6) imp (K φ) φ; (7) imp (K φ) (K (K φ)); and (8) imp (K (all x φ)) (all x (K φ))."}
translation: Target is the proposition asserting that for every set of formulas T (with no restriction on T), the formula ¬ ∃x₁ K (∀x₀ (K (¬ R₀(x₀, x₀)) ↔ R₀(x₁, x₀))) is derivable from T in the proof system Def14. More precisely, in the formal language Form (built from binary atomic formulas atom r x y indexed by natural numbers r, x, y, falsity fls, implication imp, universal quantification all x, and the unary operator K, with ¬φ defined as imp φ fls, φ ∧ ψ as ¬(imp φ (¬ψ)), φ ↔ ψ as (imp φ ψ) ∧ (imp ψ φ), and ∃x φ as ¬(all x (¬φ))), the derived formula is neg (ex 1 (K (all 0 (iff (K (neg (atom 0 0 0))) (atom 0 1 0))))), where R₀ denotes the relation with index 0, variable 0 is bound by the universal quantifier, variable 1 is bound by the existential quantifier, and the second atomic subformula has variable 1 as its first argument and variable 0 as its second argument. Derivability from T (Def14 T φ) means that φ belongs to the smallest set of formulas containing every formula in T and every axiom in Def13, and closed under modus ponens (from imp φ ψ and φ, infer ψ), with no other inference rules. Here Def13 consists of every formula obtainable by applying zero or more universal generalizations (all x) to a base axiom in Def11, together with every formula of the form K ψ where ψ is so obtainable (at most one outer application of K to such universally generalized base axioms). The base axioms (Def11) are: (1) all propositional tautologies (formulas true under every valuation v : Form → Prop with ¬ v fls and v (imp φ ψ) ↔ (v φ → v ψ)); (2) universal instantiation imp (all x φ) φ[y/x] whenever y is free for x in φ (where φ[y/x] replaces free occurrences of x with y); (3) quantifier distribution imp (all x (imp φ ψ)) (imp (all x φ) (all x ψ)); (4) vacuous quantification imp φ (all x φ) whenever x does not occur free in φ; (5) imp (K (imp φ ψ)) (imp (K φ) (K ψ)); (6) imp (K φ) φ; (7) imp (K φ) (K (K φ)); and (8) imp (K (all x φ)) (all x (K φ)).

divergences.description: Theorem 5 in P-R327 states that the schema ∃e B∀x(Bp(x) ↔ Uex) (as p(x) ranges over formulas) is inconsistent, whereas Target only states the inconsistency of the single witness instance p(x) := ¬U(x,x) used in the proof. This is a harmless strengthening (inconsistency of one instance implies inconsistency of the schema) and matches the author's stated scope.

In Reinhardt's setting, U(e, x) can be any formula with two free variables (in particular, a complex arithmetic formula), whereas Target fixes U to be a single primitive binary relation symbol (atom 0) rather than quantifying over arbitrary binary formulas (or even over relation symbol indices). Because atom 0 has no non-logical axioms, this serves as a standard schematic idealization, and the author discloses it.

The formal language and proof system (Form, Def11–Def14) omit arithmetic, equality, constants, function symbols, and predicates of arity other than 2, which are present in Reinhardt's system (P-R323). Because Theorem 5's proof does not use arithmetic or equality, this is a harmless restriction to the modal first-order fragment (declared separately by the author).

P-R323 takes universal closures (sentences) of the axiom schemas optionally prefixed by B, whereas Def12 and Def13 admit all finite (including empty and vacuous) universal generalizations of Def11, optionally prefixed by K even when open. This is deductively equivalent over modus ponens via universal instantiation, vacuous quantification, and the K-distribution/B∀ axioms.

Inconsistency of the sentence is expressed as provability of its negation from every theory T (∀ T, Def14 T (neg φ)) rather than derivability of falsehood from the sentence itself; because Def14 has only modus ponens as an inference rule, these formulations are equivalent by monotonicity and the deduction theorem.

judgement.summary: The Lean formalization faithfully captures the mathematical content of Reinhardt's Theorem 5 for the witness instance p(x) := ¬U(x,x) in an accurately formalized Hilbert-style modal first-order logic matching Reinhardt's B-axioms. Its divergences—specializing the schema to that single instance, fixing U to an atomic binary relation symbol, omitting arithmetic and equality from the language, and minor presentational differences in axiom closure and inconsistency—are all minor and largely disclosed in the claim.
